# Validation Figures: What Each Simulation Demonstrates

## Purpose

A SimItAll figure should validate a programmed mechanism against retained
simulation truth. It can demonstrate that a workflow ran as designed; it does
not by itself prove that a synthetic dataset reproduces biology in a species or
predicts clinical outcomes. Claims about realism require external data,
measured maps, appropriate reference panels, and a prespecified comparison.

## Minimum Figure Contract

Every validation figure needs a saved source-data table, explicit seed and
parameters, labelled synthetic versus supplied input, and a stated pass/fail or
interpretation criterion. Figures should be regenerated by an R script, never
manually edited.

## Breeding and Population Figures

| Question | Figure | What it checks | Expected pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Did the designed cross retain founder truth? | Founder contribution / ancestry-tract plot | Founder labels and recombination bookkeeping | Contributions and breakpoints agree with the cross design. |
| Did selfing or inbreeding raise homozygosity? | Generation-by-generation heterozygosity/homozygosity line plot and per-generation boxplot | Mendelian transmission and pedigree mechanism | Heterozygosity decreases and homozygosity increases under repeated selfing/inbreeding. |
| Did a BCn scheme recover recurrent background? | Allele-frequency or donor-fraction plot | Backcross direction and foreground selection | Donor genome fraction declines outside a selected introgression. |
| Did recombination generate plausible segments? | Segment-length density and breakpoints-per-line histogram | Map use and independent assortment | Segment and breakpoint distributions reflect the supplied map and design. |
| Is a population structured as requested? | PCA/ancestry bar plot and kinship heatmap | Subpopulation and admixture labels | Simulated groups separate only to the intended extent. |
| Is LD behaving as designed? | LD decay curve and regional LD heatmap | Haplotype/LD block generator | Stronger designed LD decays more slowly in the target region. |

The package example `analysis/paper_fig/fig10_biparental_bc2s7_allele_frequency.R`
creates the BC2S7 allele-frequency figure and its TSV source table. It is a
synthetic demonstration, not a result for named maize founders.

## GWAS and Trait Figures

| Question | Figure | What it checks | Expected pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Were causal loci recoverable? | Manhattan plot with causal loci labelled | Association-test recovery | Simulated causal loci or linked markers have stronger signals. |
| Is the association test calibrated? | QQ plot | Null p-value behavior and confounding control | Null points follow expectation except at true signals. |
| How well was truth recovered? | Power, false-positive rate, precision/recall versus threshold | Benchmark against causal truth | Metrics are computed from the saved truth table. |
| Does a trait model have the intended architecture? | Effect-size distribution and phenotype distribution | Additive/dominance/epistasis and residual variance | Distributions match the configured simulation, not a biological claim. |
| Does genomic selection work on held-out lines? | Observed-versus-predicted plot and accuracy-by-cycle curve | Leakage-aware prediction and selection cycle | Held-out correlation, gain, and diversity use separate train/test families. |

## Bulk RNA-seq and eQTL Figures

| Question | Figure | What it checks | Expected pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Did condition or batch effects enter the count model? | Sample PCA/MDS colored by condition and batch | Designed expression effects | Intended effects are visible; unwanted batch separation signals confounding. |
| Are count properties plausible for the simulation? | Mean-variance and library-size plots | Count and dispersion model | Variance rises with expression according to the configured model. |
| Were DE genes or eQTLs recovered? | Volcano plot, eQTL Manhattan plot, and truth-recovery curve | Differential-expression/eQTL benchmark | Recovery is calculated against simulated truth. |
| Was allele-specific expression programmed? | Allelic-ratio distribution by genotype | ASE mechanism | Ratios shift only for loci with simulated ASE effects. |

The executable package example is
`analysis/paper_fig/fig6_rnaseq_eqtl_simulation.R`.

## Single-Cell RNA-seq Figures

| Question | Figure | What it checks | Expected pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Did cells separate by programmed state/type? | UMAP/PCA colored by cell type, donor, condition, and batch | Cell-state and batch simulation | Labels align with retained cell metadata. |
| Were dropout and depth simulated as configured? | Zero fraction versus mean expression and library-size distribution | Technical-noise model | Dropout/depth match the specified simulation regime. |
| Did pseudobulk preserve donor replication? | Donor-by-cell-type pseudobulk heatmap | Donor/cell aggregation | Biological donors, not individual cells, are replication units. |
| Were cell-type eQTLs recovered? | Effect/recovery plot stratified by cell type | Cell-type eQTL truth benchmark | Signals appear in the programmed cell types. |

The executable package example is
`analysis/paper_fig/fig7_scrnaseq_celltype_eqtl.R`.

## Regulatory and Sequencing Figures

| Question | Figure | What it checks | Expected pattern |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Did ChIP-seq peaks use annotated regulatory targets? | Genome-track/peak-position plot | Peak placement relative to promoters/enhancers | ChIP enrichment aligns with programmed targets above input background. |
| Are ChIP and input libraries distinguishable? | Read-density profile and library-QC plot | Enrichment and read-generation logic | ChIP has target enrichment; input reflects background. |
| Does an assembly improve under a coverage/design change? | Contiguity-accuracy trade-off, genome fraction, misassembly plot | Assembly benchmark against known reference | Metrics derive from QUAST and the simulated truth reference. |
| Did read simulation achieve requested depth/length? | Coverage and read-length distribution | Read simulator parameters | Observed distributions are compared with requested settings. |

The executable ChIP-seq example is
`analysis/paper_fig/fig8_chipseq_simulation.R`. Hybrid assembly evaluation should
use a known simulated/reference genome and report QUAST output rather than a
visual claim alone.

## Interpretation Language

Use: "validates the configured mechanism," "recovers simulated truth," or
"shows agreement with the requested design." Avoid: "proves real biology,"
"demonstrates clinical risk," or "validates a named population" unless an
external, appropriately matched validation dataset is analyzed separately.
